title: for 语句和 while 语句

text: Repeat with a known count, or until a condition stops you.
A **loop** repeats its body. Before every round it checks a condition, and it stops as soon as that condition is false.
A for loop packs four parts into one line. They run in this order.
`break` leaves the innermost loop at once. `continue` skips to the next round: in a for the update still runs, in a while it does not, which can loop forever.

title: Pattern: one pass over a stream

text: Many problems need only a few **running values**, updated once per input. No array is needed when each number is used once.
`% 10` reads the last digit. `/ 10` removes it. Repeat until nothing is left.
Building `rev * 10 + digit` reverses the number, and trailing zeros vanish on their own (P1307). Use do while so that 0 still counts as one digit.
When the number of rounds is unknown, loop with while on the stopping condition and count the rounds. This solves P1423, P1035 and P1089.
Loops inside loops: rows and columns, pairs, tables.
The outer loop picks a row, the inner loop fills it. Write the inner bound in terms of the outer variable to get a **triangle**.
The counter k lives outside both loops, so it keeps counting across rows. This is P5721 and P5725.
Reset a per row counter **inside** the outer loop, not before it.
Two nested loops can also search all pairs. Here: can n be written as a² + b²?
`break` leaves only the innermost loop. To stop both, set a flag and test it in the outer condition, as above. Tighten bounds such as `a * a <= n` when you can.

title: 循环结构程序设计案例

text: Primes, divisors, brute force with filters, and how fast is fast enough.
If n = a × b with a ≤ b, then a ≤ √n. So testing divisors while `i * i <= n` is enough: O(√n) instead of O(n).
Euclid: `gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a % b)`, ending when b is 0. C++17 has `gcd(a, b)` built in.
The smallest factor of n = p × q is p, so the larger one is n / p. This is P1075.

title: Pattern: brute force with a cheap filter first

text: Put the **cheap** test (is it a palindrome? about 8 steps) before the **expensive** one (is it prime? up to √x steps). Most numbers fail the cheap test, so the slow one rarely runs.
Every palindrome with an even number of digits divides by 11, so 11 is the only prime among them. Skipping those ranges makes b up to 10⁸ fast enough (P1217).
Rule of thumb: about **10⁸** simple operations per second. Estimate the loop count from the limits before you write code.
